predecessors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: Mértola and its district, independent at the downfall of the Caliphate of Córdoba

successors.name: Almohad Caliphate
successors.text: Mértola, 'finally conquered by the Almohad Caliphate' in 1151; Almohad 1151-1250

rulers.name: Abu-l-Qasim Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Qasi
Abu-l-Qasim Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Qasi, restored

ledger.x: 1144: Mértola is independent again under Ibn Qasi, a mystic and military leader who 'fought the power of the Almoravides' (Mértola page: 'Between 1144 and 1150 the town was again seat of an independent state led by Ibn Qasi').
1145: 'Badajoz period: 1145-1146' on the Taifa page; the page does not say how it passed.
1146: Ibn Qasi is 'restored 1146-1151' (Taifa page ruler list).
1151: 'Its short-lived history ended in 1151, when it was finally conquered by the Almohad Caliphate' (Almohad 1151-1250); Ibn Qasi died in 1151 (Ibn Qasi page).
1151: the Taifa of Mértola ends; the Portuguese took the town in 1238.

wars.name: Revolt of Ibn Qasi
wars.outcome: Ibn Qasi's followers (murid revolt) made Mértola and Silves independent of the Almoravids in 1144; he rebelled with Portuguese help against the Almohads and was beheaded by his own followers in 1151.

certainty.note: The pages name Mértola only; the 20 km circle echoes the modern municipality's area.
